text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: GPU pool 'eu-west-1a-gpu' capacity_exhausted. Autoscaler reports repeated scale failures (quota/limit) and queue growth observed across gpu-ingest and realtime routes. Paging on-call. thread_ts=1767777000

alex: i'm on it. seeing 95% pool utilization and steady enqueue rate. controller logs show 'scaleup rejected: provider quota' repeated. starting triage.

maria: i’ll pull the autoscaler logs + recent operator events. can someone confirm which customers are seeing 429s? lia?

lia: customer-success: flags from two larger tenants — elevated 429/latency for embedding calls since ~09:12 UTC. I’m DMing affected CSMs and will post updates.

carter: runtime: primaries are hitting the 4-gpu-per-pool soft cap from the provider. autoscaler tried to request extra nodes but API returned 403 quota_exceeded. there are also ~40 low-priority jobs queued in burst-pool.

june: oncall: can we triage to reduce queue pressure? options: 1) route non-critical tenants to fallback model variant (cpu/quantized), 2) pause background batch jobs, 3) manual eviction of lower priority queues. Thoughts?

alex: do option 1 + 2 now. can we flip route for embeddings for tenants with graceful degradation? carter, can you write the routing override?

carter: preparing quick route rule: ```
# temporary route override
route: embeddings
match: tenant in ["non-prod","platinum-grace"]
action: model_variant=redwood-embed-quantized-1
ttl: 30m
```
I’ll deploy to edge now.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated by carter for route override to env=prod. build 2026.3.17677 -> 17677. status: rolling.

maria: autoscaler logs (snippet): ```
2026-03-15T09:14:22Z autoscaler: attempt_scale_up request_id=aa2f status=failed reason=quota_exceeded provider_resp={"code":403,"message":"quota exceeded for region eu-west-1a"}
2026-03-15T09:15:10Z autoscaler: attempt_scale_up request_id=aa2g status=failed reason=quota_exceeded
2026-03-15T09:16:05Z controller: backoff increased to 30s
```

ajex: (reaction :eyes:) — (note: alex alias for this thread)

june: ops-bot, can we drain low priority queue tasks?

ops-bot: action queued: evict_tasks queue=burst-pool priority<=low limit=40 initiated_by=june. ETA 45s.

lia: CSM update sent: "We’re seeing degraded performance for embeddings for a subset of customers. We’ve applied temporary fallbacks and are evicting low-priority jobs. Next update in 15 minutes."

alex: traffic routing change applied. initial metrics show 30% drop in enqueue to gpu pool, tail latency for critical tenants improving. still seeing some 429s for queued realtime requests.

carter: i can attempt a manual scaling action via provider console as an emergency: request 2 additional g4dn nodes in separate AZ (eu-west-1b) and wire them to the pool as a temporary measure. need approval.

maria: confirm provider quotas first — if quota is global per project then adding in another AZ may fail. i’ll run the quota-check script: ```
./tools/check_provider_quota.sh --region eu-west-1
# output
GPU quota total: 10
GPU allocated: 10
GPU available: 0
```

carter: ok quota is indeed at limit. ops request to cloud team for quota bump. who can ping provider support directly?

alex: i’ll contact cloud-ops and request an emergency quota bump. posting request in cloud-support channel and contacting provider slack.

alex: message -> @cloud-ops: emergency quota bump needed for eu-west-1 gpu quota; 2 GPUs immediate. incident ref=1767777000. attaching logs and justification.

cloud-ops (via channel): acked. opened support ticket INC-98321, escalation to 'P1 quota increase'. ETA 30-60m.

maria: in parallel, we should add a short-circuit fallback in router: if queue latency > 500ms then return queued with Retry-After and route to cpu-embed variant. reduces 429 tail. carter can you put that in?

carter: added a short-circuit: ```
if queue_latency_ms > 500:
  respond 429 Retry-After=10
  route model_variant=redwood-embed-cpu-approx
```
Deploying.

deploy-bot: deploy complete. routing short-circuit active.

june: monitoring dashboards: enqueue rate down 45%, pool utilization 88% now (was 96%), 429 rate cut by ~60% for non-critical tenants. critical customers still seeing intermittent 429s (peak window during 09:10-09:18).

lia: customers acknowledged. one priority customer requested an internal blameless postmortem and timeline. I told them yes — we’ll share a summary after incident.

alex: action items for immediate mitigation summary: 1) applied route fallback 2) evicted low-priority queue 3) short-circuit for high queue latency 4) requested provider quota bump 5) manual scale if quota approved.

maria: can we schedule a bridgecall if cloud support ETA slips beyond 45m? want runtime + oncall + product leads on it.

alex: agree. if no quota increase by 09:55 UTC -> bridgecall. setting timer.

ops-bot: timer set for 1767777300 (09:55 UTC).

-- 25 minutes later --

cloud-ops: update from provider: quota bump approved. provisioning 2x g4dn nodes in eu-west-1b. expected ready in ~6 minutes.

carter: manual attach script ready: ```
./scripts/attach_node.sh --node-id $PROVIDER_NODE_123 --pool eu-west-1a-gpu
```
I’ll run after nodes are Ready.

deploy-bot: provider nodes transitioned to Ready.

carter: attached nodes to pool. autoscaler recalculated. queue backlog cleared over next 120s.

june: monitoring: 429s returned to baseline, latency normalized. queue length at near-zero. excellent.

lia: CSM update: "Issue mitigated. We added temporary fallbacks and scaled capacity while provider quota increased. No data loss. Follow-up postmortem will be shared."

alex: immediate incident summary for postmortem notes: root cause: provider GPU quota exhausted + autoscaler did not have a fast path for fallback when quota_exceeded (it kept backing off). Contributing: large concurrent ingest from background batch jobs and missing pre-warm buffer.

maria: proposed postmortem action items: - request permanent quota increase for prod projects in eu-west-1 - add a hot standby pool (pre-warmed 1-2 GPUs) in a separate AZ - change autoscaler policy: on quota_exceeded -> attempt cross-AZ scale / manual escalate flag + stop exponential backoff for first 2 retries - update alerting: queue-growth alert should include provider quota_saturation metric - update runbook with exact commands used here and who to page in cloud-support channel

carter: tech tasks I’ll take: implement short-circuit permanently as toggleable feature; add router rule generator for per-tenant graceful degradation; implement cross-AZ attach automation.

alex: I’ll own comms + postmortem write-up and runbook update. june will own incident review with oncall rotation changes. lia will coordinate customer comms. maria will file the cloud quota tickets and own verification.

june: adding timeline and notes to incident board. planning retrospective 48 hours from now.

lia: thanks everyone — closing pager for now. will reopen if anomalies recur.

incidents-bot: incident status -> resolved (mitigated). duration 00:44:20. participants: alex, maria, carter, june, lia, cloud-ops.

-- POST-INCIDENT QUICK NOTES --

alex: quick note for postmortem: add runbook snippet used to evict low-priority tasks: ```./tools/evict_queue --queue burst-pool --priority <= low --limit 40```

maria: logs + timeline saved to /incidents/1767777000/artifacts (metrics graphs, autoscaler logs, provider ticket).

carter: opened follow-up tasks in backlog: RD-1245 (hot-standby pool), RD-1246 (cross-az attach automation), RD-1247 (router graceful-degrade toggle).

june: retro scheduled: 2026-03-17 14:00 UTC. invite: eng-runtime, eng-sre, cloud-ops, product ops, customer-success.

lia: i'll draft a customer-facing summary and share before the retro.

alex: closing thread. thanks team. :thumbsup:
